---
# site-compute.yml -- provision Slurm compute + GPU nodes on larch
# Research Computing Services, University of Northfield
#
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/larch/hosts.ini site-compute.yml --limit 'gpu[01:08]' --diff --check
#
# NB:  slurm_version MUST match the controller (group_vars/slurmctld.yml), otherwise slurmd refuses to register.
# NB2: slurmdbd_password is vaulted -> run with --ask-vault-pass or export ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE

- name: Configure Slurm compute nodes
  hosts: compute:gpu:!drained
  become: yes
  gather_facts: true
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10
  vars_files:
    - vars/slurm.yml
    - "vars/{{ cluster_name }}-secrets.yml"
  vars:
    slurm_version: "24.05.4"
    slurm_user: { name: slurm, uid: 981,  gid: 981 }
    spack_root: /opt/spack
    lmod_version: 8.7.53
    scratch_root:   /scratch
    drain_first: True
    # Rendered into slurm.conf.j2 (one PartitionName= line each). Keep the columns lined up, it makes --diff readable.
    slurm_partitions:
      # fmt: table
      - {name: short, nodes: "cn[001-120]", max_time: "04:00:00", default: true, tier: 10}
      - {name: long,   nodes: "cn[001-096]",  max_time: "7-00:00:00", default: false, tier: 5}
      - {name: gpu, nodes: "gpu[01-08]", max_time: '2-00:00:00', default: false, tier: 10}
      - {name: bigmem, nodes: "fat[1-4]", max_time: 3-00:00:00, default: no, tier: 5}
    gres_types: [a100, h100]
    cgroup_conf: |
      CgroupPlugin=cgroup/v2
      ConstrainCores=yes
      ConstrainRAMSpace=yes
      ConstrainDevices=yes
      AllowedRAMSpace=98
    nhc:
      enabled: yes
      interval: 300     # seconds; NHC also runs as slurmd's HealthCheckProgram
      checks: [ check_fs_mount_rw -f /scratch, check_fs_mount_rw -f /home, 'check_hw_ib 100', check_ps_service -u root -S sshd ]
    slurmdbd_password: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          36383433643335336339626631616532373731363266306566343634396137653262363931393630
          3630356261353637663538656630333366386334373562320a383463613033383432643039383662
          30623234616565373939386139313737303436656235306432636636356137323533393537343366
          3564633366643938310a316131623662326139663466646237306462653564313765383233626632
          6237

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refuse to run on anything that is not EL9
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - ansible_distribution in ['Rocky', 'AlmaLinux', 'RedHat']
          - ansible_distribution_major_version | int >= 9
        fail_msg: "larch compute images are EL9 only (got {{ ansible_distribution }} {{ ansible_distribution_version }})"
        quiet: true

    - name: Drain node before touching slurmd
      command: scontrol update NodeName={{ inventory_hostname_short }} State=DRAIN Reason="ansible run {{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 }}"
      delegate_to: "{{ groups['slurmctld'][0] }}"
      changed_when: false
      when: drain_first | bool

  tasks:
    - name: Install Slurm, munge and friends
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name:
          - "slurm-{{ slurm_version }}"
          - "slurm-slurmd-{{ slurm_version }}"
          - "slurm-pam_slurm-{{ slurm_version }}"
          - munge
          - hwloc
          - numactl
          - lua-posix        # Lmod
          - "nhc >= 1.4.3"
        state: present
        enablerepo: larch-hpc,epel
      notify: restart slurmd

    - name: Munge key
      copy:
        src: files/munge.key
        dest: /etc/munge/munge.key
        owner: munge
        group: munge
        mode: 0400
      no_log: true
      notify:
      - restart munge

    - name: Slurm config files
      template: src={{ item }}.j2 dest=/etc/slurm/{{ item }} owner=root group=root mode=0644
      loop:
        - slurm.conf
        - gres.conf
        - topology.conf
      notify: restart slurmd

    - name: cgroup.conf
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: "{{ cgroup_conf }}"
        dest: /etc/slurm/cgroup.conf
        mode: '0644'
      notify: restart slurmd

    - name: Per-job scratch cleanup epilog
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/slurm/epilog.d/50-scratch-cleanup.sh
        mode: "0755"
        # !unsafe because ${#dirs[@]} looks like the start of a Jinja comment to Ansible
        content: !unsafe |
          #!/bin/bash
          # Runs as root on every node of the allocation after the job has ended.
          [[ -n "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" ]] || exit 0
          dirs=( "/scratch/local/job.${SLURM_JOB_ID}" "/dev/shm/job.${SLURM_JOB_ID}" )
          logger -t slurm-epilog "removing ${#dirs[@]} scratch dirs for job ${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
          rm -rf --one-file-system -- "${dirs[@]}"
          exit 0

    - name: GPU nodes
      when:
        - "'gpu' in group_names"
        - ansible_local.nvidia.driver_version is defined
      block:
        - name: Install DCGM
          ansible.builtin.dnf: {name: datacenter-gpu-manager, state: present}

        - name: Persistence mode + DCGM host engine
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: "{{ item }}"
            enabled: true
            state: started
          loop: [nvidia-persistenced, nvidia-dcgm]

        - name: Quick GPU diagnostic (dcgmi diag -r 1)
          ansible.builtin.command: dcgmi diag -r 1 -j
          register: dcgm_diag
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: >-
            (dcgm_diag.stdout | from_json).DCGM_GPU_DIAGNOSTIC.test_categories
            | map(attribute='tests') | flatten | selectattr('results', 'search', 'Fail') | list | length > 0
      rescue:
        - name: Keep the node drained so nobody lands on a broken GPU
          ansible.builtin.command: >
            scontrol update NodeName={{ inventory_hostname_short }}
            State=DRAIN Reason="dcgm diag failed {{ ansible_date_time.date }}"
          delegate_to: "{{ groups['slurmctld'][0] }}"
        - ansible.builtin.meta: end_host

    - name: Spack upstream for user installs
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: "{{ spack_root }}/etc/spack/upstreams.yaml"
        mode: "0644"
        content: |
          upstreams:
            larch-central:
              install_tree: /opt/spack/opt/spack
              modules:
                lmod: /opt/spack/share/spack/lmod
      tags: [spack]

    - name: Lmod default MODULEPATH
      lineinfile:
        path: /etc/profile.d/z00_lmod.sh
        regexp: '^export MODULEPATH='
        line: 'export MODULEPATH=/opt/spack/share/spack/lmod/linux-rocky9-x86_64/Core:/opt/modulefiles'
        create: yes
      tags: [ spack,lmod ]

    - meta: flush_handlers

    - name: Undrain
      command: scontrol update NodeName={{ inventory_hostname_short }} State=RESUME
      delegate_to: "{{ groups['slurmctld'][0] }}"
      when: drain_first | bool

  handlers:
    - name: restart munge
      service: name=munge state=restarted
    - name: restart slurmd
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: slurmd
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: yes


- name: Login nodes | news file shown by `larch-news`
  hosts: login
  become: true
  tags: [news]
  vars_files: [vars/slurm.yml]
  vars:
    maint_window: {start: "Wed 2 Dec 06:00", end: "Fri 4 Dec 18:00"}
  tasks:
    - name: /etc/larch/news.md (rendered in the terminal with glow)
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/larch/news.md
        owner: root
        mode: "0644"
        # fmt: markdown
        content: |
          # larch news ({{ ansible_date_time.date }})

          **Maintenance:** the `long` and `bigmem` partitions will be drained from {{ maint_window.start }} until {{ maint_window.end }}. Jobs that cannot finish before the window starts stay pending with reason `ReqNodeNotAvail, Reserved for maintenance` -- they are *not* cancelled.

          * Slurm is now {{ slurm_version }}. Job scripts that set both `--mem` and `--mem-per-cpu` are rejected at submission time, pick one.
          *   GPU jobs must ask for a GPU type explicitly, e.g. `--gres=gpu:a100:2`; an untyped `--gres=gpu:2` now lands on the (much slower) V100 nodes in `gpu-legacy`.
          * `/scratch` is **not** backed up and files older than 60 days are purged every Sunday night.

          Questions: <rcs-help@northfield.ac.uk> or the [user guide](https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/).

# docker-compose.yml for cmorph-pp -- CMIP6 post-processing stack (dev / single workstation)
# Climate Analytics Group, Dept. of Earth System Science, University of Northfield
#
#   cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d
#   docker compose --profile thredds up -d       # also serve the outputs over OPeNDAP
#   docker compose run --rm pp-cli regrid --source-id MPI-ESM1-2-HR --experiment ssp585 --grid 1x1
#
# The ESGF mirror lives on the group NFS (/data/cmip6, read-only). Do NOT bind-mount it rw: the export is
# shared with the larch cluster and a stray `rm -rf` in a container takes out everyone's replicas.

name: cmorph-pp

x-common-env: &common-env
  TZ: UTC
  OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"            # dask does the parallelism, don't let MKL/OpenBLAS oversubscribe
  MKL_NUM_THREADS: '1'
  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: 1
  HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING: "FALSE"  # NFS + HDF5 file locking = hung workers
  DASK_DISTRIBUTED__COMM__TIMEOUTS__CONNECT: 60s
  DASK_TEMPORARY_DIRECTORY: /scratch/dask-tmp
  ESMFMKFILE: /opt/conda/lib/esmf.mk

x-logging: &logging
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options: {max-size: "50m", max-file: "5"}

x-data-volumes: &data-volumes
  - type: bind
    source: ${CMIP6_ROOT:-/data/cmip6}
    target: /data/cmip6
    read_only: true
  - type: volume
    source: scratch
    target: /scratch
  - ./config:/etc/cmorph-pp:ro

x-worker: &worker
  image: ghcr.io/nfld-climate/cmorph-pp:${PP_TAG:-2026.11.0}
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment:
    <<: *common-env
    DASK_DISTRIBUTED__WORKER__MEMORY__TARGET: 0.6
    DASK_DISTRIBUTED__WORKER__MEMORY__SPILL: 0.7
    DASK_DISTRIBUTED__WORKER__MEMORY__PAUSE: 0.85
    DASK_DISTRIBUTED__WORKER__MEMORY__TERMINATE: 0.95
  volumes: *data-volumes
  depends_on:
    scheduler:
      condition: service_healthy
  command: >
    dask worker tcp://scheduler:8786
    --nworkers 1 --nthreads ${WORKER_THREADS:-4}
    --memory-limit ${WORKER_MEMORY:-16GiB}
    --local-directory /scratch/dask-tmp
    --name $${HOSTNAME}
  stop_grace_period: 1m30s

services:

  scheduler:
    <<: *logging
    image: ghcr.io/nfld-climate/cmorph-pp:${PP_TAG:-2026.11.0}
    command: ["dask", "scheduler", "--port", "8786", "--dashboard-address", ":8787"]
    environment: *common-env
    ports:
      - "8786:8786"
      - 127.0.0.1:8787:8787     # dashboard, localhost only -- use ssh -L from your laptop
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "python -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection((\"localhost\", 8786), 2)'" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 20s

  worker-a:
    <<: [*worker, *logging]
    hostname: worker-a
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: "4", memory: 18g}

  worker-b:
    <<: [ *worker, *logging ]
    hostname: worker-b
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
            cpus: '4'
            memory: 18g

  # GPU worker: builds the conservative regridding weights with xESMF + cupy.
  # Only on hosts with nvidia-container-toolkit, hence the profile.
  worker-gpu:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: ["gpu"]
    hostname: worker-gpu
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "0"
      CMORPH_ARRAY_BACKEND: cupy
      DASK_DISTRIBUTED__WORKER__RESOURCES__GPU: 1
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
          - driver: nvidia
            count: 1
            capabilities: [gpu]

  jupyter:
    <<: *logging
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile.jupyter
      args:
        PYTHON_VERSION: "3.12"
        ESMF_VERSION: 8.7.0
        XESMF_VERSION: 0.8.8
    ports: [ 8888:8888 ]
    volumes:
      - ${CMIP6_ROOT:-/data/cmip6}:/data/cmip6:ro
      - scratch:/scratch
      - ./notebooks:/home/jovyan/work
      - pp-output:/data/output
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      JUPYTER_TOKEN: ${JUPYTER_TOKEN:?set JUPYTER_TOKEN in .env}
      DASK_SCHEDULER_ADDRESS: tcp://scheduler:8786
      JUPYTER_ENABLE_LAB:
    user: "${UID:-1000}:${GID:-100}"
    depends_on: [scheduler]

  thredds:
    image: unidata/thredds-docker:5.5
    profiles:
      - thredds
    ports:
      - target: 8080
        published: "8081"
        protocol: tcp
        mode: host
    environment:
      - TDS_CONTENT_ROOT_PATH=/usr/local/tomcat/content
      - TDM_PW=${TDM_PW}
      - "JAVA_OPTS=-Xms4g -Xmx8g -server -Djava.awt.headless=true"
      - TDS_HOST=http://localhost:8081
    volumes:
      - ./thredds/catalog.xml:/usr/local/tomcat/content/thredds/catalog.xml:ro
      - type: volume
        source: pp-output
        target: /data/output
        read_only: true
        volume: {nocopy: true}

  pp-cli:
    image: ghcr.io/nfld-climate/cmorph-pp:${PP_TAG:-2026.11.0}
    profiles: [cli]
    entrypoint: ["cmorph-pp"]
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      DASK_SCHEDULER_ADDRESS: tcp://scheduler:8786
    volumes: *data-volumes
    working_dir: /scratch
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true
    labels:
      org.opencontainers.image.description: "CLI for regridding, de-drifting and CMORizing CMIP6 output; see docs/pp-cli.md"
      uk.ac.northfield.climate.maintainer: 'Dr. A. Lindqvist <a.lindqvist@northfield.ac.uk>'

volumes:
  scratch:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: tmpfs
      device: tmpfs
      o: "size=64g,uid=1000"
  pp-output:
    external: true

# CI for fernsolve: builds the C++ core + Python bindings against several MPI / BLAS combinations
# and runs the convergence regression suite. The nightly run also does a strong-scaling smoke test
# on the self-hosted runner that lives on a larch login node (yes, really -- RCS signed it off, see #741).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron:  '17 3 * * *'     # 03:17 UTC, off the hour to dodge the GitHub cron stampede
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_scaling:
        description: Run the strong-scaling smoke test on the self-hosted larch runner (needs a 4-node allocation, ~40 min)
        type: boolean
        default: false
      rtol:
        description: "Relative residual tolerance for the regression suite"
        required: false
        default: '1e-10'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL: 4
  CTEST_OUTPUT_ON_FAILURE: 1
  OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: "yes"     # runners have 4 vCPUs, the MPI tests use up to 8 ranks
  PRTE_MCA_rmaps_default_mapping_policy: ':oversubscribe'
  FERN_TEST_RTOL: ${{ inputs.rtol || '1e-10' }}

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - &checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0     # setuptools-scm needs the tags
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '3.12', cache: pip}
      - run: pip install pre-commit && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

  build-test:
    name: ${{ matrix.os }} / ${{ matrix.compiler }} / ${{ matrix.mpi }}${{ matrix.blas && format(' / {0}', matrix.blas) || '' }}
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-22.04,
             macos-14]
        compiler: [gcc, clang]
        mpi: [openmpi, mpich]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-14
            mpi: mpich       # Homebrew mpich + Apple clang: Fortran ABI mismatch, see #812
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, compiler: clang}
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-24.04
            compiler: gcc
            mpi: openmpi
            blas: openblas-openmp
            coverage: true
          - os: ubuntu-24.04
            compiler: intel-oneapi
            mpi: intelmpi
            blas: mkl
            experimental: true
    steps:
      - *checkout

      - name: Install toolchain (Ubuntu)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && matrix.compiler != 'intel-oneapi'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          case "${{ matrix.mpi }}" in
            openmpi) MPI_PKGS="libopenmpi-dev openmpi-bin" ;;
            mpich)   MPI_PKGS="libmpich-dev mpich" ;;
          esac
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ninja-build $MPI_PKGS \
               libopenblas-openmp-dev liblapacke-dev libsuitesparse-dev

      - name: Install toolchain (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: brew install ninja open-mpi openblas suite-sparse

      - name: Install Intel oneAPI
        if: matrix.compiler == 'intel-oneapi'
        uses: rscohn2/setup-oneapi@v0
        with:
          components: |
            icx@2025.0.4
            impi@2021.14.1
            mkl@2025.0.1

      - name: Configure
        shell: bash
        run: >
          cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
          -DFERN_ENABLE_MPI=ON
          -DFERN_BLAS_VENDOR=${{ matrix.blas || 'Generic' }}
          -DFERN_ENABLE_COVERAGE=${{ matrix.coverage && 'ON' || 'OFF' }}
          -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${{ matrix.compiler == 'gcc' && 'gcc' || matrix.compiler == 'clang' && 'clang' || 'icx' }}
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${{ matrix.compiler == 'gcc' && 'g++' || matrix.compiler == 'clang' && 'clang++' || 'icpx' }}

      - name: Build
        run: cmake --build build --target all fernsolve_python

      - name: Unit + MPI tests (1/2/4/8 ranks)
        working-directory: build
        run: ctest -L 'unit|mpi' --timeout 900 -j2
        env:
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: 1

      - name: Convergence regression suite
        run: |
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]" --no-build-isolation
          pytest tests/regression -q -n auto --rtol "$FERN_TEST_RTOL" \
            --junitxml=reports/regression-${{ strategy.job-index }}.xml
          {
            echo "### Regression summary (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.mpi }})"
            echo
            echo "| matrix | solver | iters | rel. residual |"
            echo "|---|---|---:|---:|"
            python tools/summarize_regression.py reports/ --format md-rows
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Upload coverage
        if: ${{ matrix.coverage && !cancelled() }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          flags: ${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.mpi }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  scaling-smoke:
    # Self-hosted runner `larch-login2` submits a 4-node job via sbatch and waits for it.
    # Only on schedule or manual dispatch, NEVER on pull_request (forks could run arbitrary code on the cluster)
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_scaling)
    needs: [ build-test ]
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, larch]
    timeout-minutes: 120
    env:
      SBATCH_ACCOUNT: rse-fernsolve
      SBATCH_PARTITION: short
      SBATCH_TIMELIMIT: "00:45:00"
      SBATCH_EXCLUSIVE: 1
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - name: Submit and wait
        id: submit
        run: |
          module purge
          module load gcc/13.2.0 openmpi/4.1.6 cmake/3.29.2 openblas/0.3.27
          jobid=$(sbatch --parsable --wait --nodes=4 --ntasks-per-node=64 --cpus-per-task=3 \
                    --output=scaling-%j.out ci/slurm/strong_scaling.sbatch)
          echo "jobid=${jobid}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          sacct -j "$jobid" --format=JobID,Elapsed,MaxRSS,State%20 -P | column -t -s '|'
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: scaling-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            scaling-*.out
            build/scaling/*.csv
          retention-days: 14

# Genomics core -- k8s manifests for the variant-calling stack on the `okapi` research cluster.
# Rendered base for `kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/prod`. Do not hand-edit in prod, edit deploy/base/*.yaml.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:

# CI for fernsolve: builds the C++ core + Python bindings against several MPI / BLAS combinations
# and runs the convergence regression suite. The nightly run also does a strong-scaling smoke test
# on the self-hosted runner that lives on a larch login node (yes, really -- RCS signed it off, see #741).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron:  '17 3 * * *'     # 03:17 UTC, off the hour to dodge the GitHub cron stampede
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_scaling:
        description: Run the strong-scaling smoke test on the self-hosted larch runner (needs a 4-node allocation, ~40 min)
        type: boolean
        default: false
      rtol:
        description: "Relative residual tolerance for the regression suite"
        required: false
        default: '1e-10'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL: 4
  CTEST_OUTPUT_ON_FAILURE: 1
  OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: "yes"     # runners have 4 vCPUs, the MPI tests use up to 8 ranks
  PRTE_MCA_rmaps_default_mapping_policy: ':oversubscribe'
  FERN_TEST_RTOL: ${{ inputs.rtol || '1e-10' }}

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - &checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0     # setuptools-scm needs the tags
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '3.12', cache: pip}
      - run: pip install pre-commit && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

  build-test:
    name: ${{ matrix.os }} / ${{ matrix.compiler }} / ${{ matrix.mpi }}${{ matrix.blas && format(' / {0}', matrix.blas) || '' }}
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-22.04,
             macos-14]
        compiler: [gcc, clang]
        mpi: [openmpi, mpich]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-14
            mpi: mpich       # Homebrew mpich + Apple clang: Fortran ABI mismatch, see #812
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, compiler: clang}
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-24.04
            compiler: gcc
            mpi: openmpi
            blas: openblas-openmp
            coverage: true
          - os: ubuntu-24.04
            compiler: intel-oneapi
            mpi: intelmpi
            blas: mkl
            experimental: true
    steps:
      - *checkout

      - name: Install toolchain (Ubuntu)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && matrix.compiler != 'intel-oneapi'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          case "${{ matrix.mpi }}" in
            openmpi) MPI_PKGS="libopenmpi-dev openmpi-bin" ;;
            mpich)   MPI_PKGS="libmpich-dev mpich" ;;
          esac
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ninja-build $MPI_PKGS \
               libopenblas-openmp-dev liblapacke-dev libsuitesparse-dev

      - name: Install toolchain (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: brew install ninja open-mpi openblas suite-sparse

      - name: Install Intel oneAPI
        if: matrix.compiler == 'intel-oneapi'
        uses: rscohn2/setup-oneapi@v0
        with:
          components: |
            icx@2025.0.4
            impi@2021.14.1
            mkl@2025.0.1

      - name: Configure
        shell: bash
        run: >
          cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
          -DFERN_ENABLE_MPI=ON
          -DFERN_BLAS_VENDOR=${{ matrix.blas || 'Generic' }}
          -DFERN_ENABLE_COVERAGE=${{ matrix.coverage && 'ON' || 'OFF' }}
          -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${{ matrix.compiler == 'gcc' && 'gcc' || matrix.compiler == 'clang' && 'clang' || 'icx' }}
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${{ matrix.compiler == 'gcc' && 'g++' || matrix.compiler == 'clang' && 'clang++' || 'icpx' }}

      - name: Build
        run: cmake --build build --target all fernsolve_python

      - name: Unit + MPI tests (1/2/4/8 ranks)
        working-directory: build
        run: ctest -L 'unit|mpi' --timeout 900 -j2
        env:
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: 1

      - name: Convergence regression suite
        run: |
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]" --no-build-isolation
          pytest tests/regression -q -n auto --rtol "$FERN_TEST_RTOL" \
            --junitxml=reports/regression-${{ strategy.job-index }}.xml
          {
            echo "### Regression summary (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.mpi }})"
            echo
            echo "| matrix | solver | iters | rel. residual |"
            echo "|---|---|---:|---:|"
            python tools/summarize_regression.py reports/ --format md-rows
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Upload coverage
        if: ${{ matrix.coverage && !cancelled() }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          flags: ${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.mpi }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  scaling-smoke:
    # Self-hosted runner `larch-login2` submits a 4-node job via sbatch and waits for it.
    # Only on schedule or manual dispatch, NEVER on pull_request (forks could run arbitrary code on the cluster)
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_scaling)
    needs: [ build-test ]
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, larch]
    timeout-minutes: 120
    env:
      SBATCH_ACCOUNT: rse-fernsolve
      SBATCH_PARTITION: short
      SBATCH_TIMELIMIT: "00:45:00"
      SBATCH_EXCLUSIVE: 1
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - name: Submit and wait
        id: submit
        run: |
          module purge
          module load gcc/13.2.0 openmpi/4.1.6 cmake/3.29.2 openblas/0.3.27
          jobid=$(sbatch --parsable --wait --nodes=4 --ntasks-per-node=64 --cpus-per-task=3 \
                    --output=scaling-%j.out ci/slurm/strong_scaling.sbatch)
          echo "jobid=${jobid}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          sacct -j "$jobid" --format=JobID,Elapsed,MaxRSS,State%20 -P | column -t -s '|'
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: scaling-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            scaling-*.out
            build/scaling/*.csv
          retention-days: 14

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: larch Compute Gateway API
  version: "2.3.0"
  summary: Submit and monitor Slurm jobs on the larch cluster from science gateways and workflow engines.
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The Compute Gateway lets **trusted science gateways** (Galaxy, the Northfield JupyterHub, Nextflow Tower) submit Slurm batch jobs on behalf of a user without that user ever handing over an SSH key. Every request carries an OAuth 2.0 access token issued to the *gateway*; the `X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of` header names the end user, who must have authorised the gateway once at <https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/gateways>.

    ## Limits

    | Limit | Value | Notes |
    |---|---|---|
    | Requests per minute per gateway | 600 | `429` with `Retry-After` when exceeded |
    | Pending jobs per user via the gateway | 2,000 | an array counts as one job per task |
    | Max. script size | 64 KiB | |

    Job scripts are passed to `sbatch` **unchanged**, so `#SBATCH` lines in the script win over fields in the request body -- except `account` and `partition`, which the gateway always enforces (cf. the [RCS acceptable use policy](https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/policies/aup/)).
  contact:
    name: Research Computing Services
    email: rcs-help@northfield.ac.uk
    url: https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/
  license: {name: Apache 2.0, identifier: Apache-2.0}

servers: # fmt: table
  - {url: "https://gateway.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2", description: Production (larch)}
  - {url: https://gateway-staging.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2, description: "Staging, talks to the 8-node test partition"}
  - {url: 'http://localhost:8080/v2', description: Local dev}

tags:
  - name: Cluster
  - name: Jobs
    description: Submission, state and cancellation.
  - {name: Accounting, description: Usage and fairshare}

security:
  - gatewayOAuth: [jobs:submit, jobs:read]

paths:
  /partitions:
    get:
      operationId: listPartitions
      tags: [Cluster]
      summary: List partitions visible to the user
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OnBehalfOf'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Partitions with current availability.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Partition"}
        "401": {$ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'}

  /jobs:
    post:
      operationId: submitJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Submit a batch job
      # fmt: markdown
      description: >-
        Submits `script` with `sbatch --parsable`. The response is returned as soon as Slurm has accepted the job, i.e. **before** it starts; poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` or, better, register a `callbackUrl` and the gateway will POST the final state to it.

        Array jobs: set `array` to a Slurm index expression such as `0-99%10`. Each task is then addressable as `{jobId}_{taskId}`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OnBehalfOf'
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false
          description: Re-sending a request with the same key within 24 h returns the original job instead of submitting a duplicate.
          schema: {type: string, format: uuid}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'}
            examples:
              gromacs:
                summary: 4-node GROMACS run
                value:
                  name: lysozyme-npt
                  account: chem-md-2026
                  partition: short
                  nodes: 4
                  ntasksPerNode: 64
                  timeLimit: "02:00:00"
                  script: |
                    #!/bin/bash
                    module load gromacs/2024.3-ompi
                    srun gmx_mpi mdrun -deffnm npt -maxh 1.9
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Accepted by Slurm.
          headers:
            Location: {schema: {type: string, format: uri}, description: URL of the new job resource}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '400': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: Python
          label: requests
          # fmt: python
          source: |
            import os, requests
            tok=os.environ["LARCH_TOKEN"]
            r=requests.post("https://gateway.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2/jobs",headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {tok}","X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of":"abc123"},json={"name":"test","account":"chem-md-2026","script":"#!/bin/bash\nhostname\n"},timeout=30)
            r.raise_for_status(); print(r.json()["jobId"])
        - lang: Shell
          label: curl
          source: |
            curl -sS -X POST "$LARCH_GATEWAY/v2/jobs" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $LARCH_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d @job.json

  /jobs/{jobId}:
    parameters:
      - name: jobId
        in: path
        required: true
        description: Slurm job ID, or `<arrayJobId>_<taskId>` for an array task.
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: '^\d+(_\d+)?$'
          examples: ["4815162", 4815162_42]
    get:
      operationId: getJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Job state and accounting
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
    delete:
      operationId: cancelJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Cancel (scancel) a job
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: signal
          schema: {type: string, enum: [TERM, KILL, USR1, USR2], default: TERM}
      responses:
        '202': {description: Signal sent.}
        '409':
          description: Job already finished.

  /usage/{account}:
    get:
      operationId: getUsage
      tags: [Accounting]
      summary: Core-hour usage and fairshare for a Slurm account
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Returns raw usage in core-hours (GPU-hours are reported separately and weighted ×4 in the billing TRES) and the account's current fairshare factor, computed with Slurm's classic algorithm as

        $$F = 2^{-U_{\mathrm{eff}}/S_{\mathrm{norm}}}$$

        where $U_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective (decayed, half-life 14 days) usage and $S_{\mathrm{norm}}$ the normalised shares. A value of `0.5` means the account has used exactly its share; values near `0` mean jobs from this account wait behind everybody else's.
      parameters:
        - {name: account, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,31}$'}}
        - name: since
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date}
          example: 2026-10-01
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Usage summary.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Usage'}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    gatewayOAuth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://login.northfield.ac.uk/realms/hpc/protocol/openid-connect/token
          scopes:
            jobs:submit: Submit jobs on behalf of authorised users
            jobs:read: Read job state and output
            'usage:read': Read accounting data
  parameters:
    OnBehalfOf:
      name: X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Northfield username (`abc123`) of the end user.
      schema: {type: string, pattern: "^[a-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$"}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or expired token.
    Problem:
      description: RFC 9457 problem details.
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    JobState:
      type: string
      enum: [PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMEOUT, OUT_OF_MEMORY, NODE_FAIL, PREEMPTED]
    JobSubmission:
      type: object
      required: [name, account, script]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 128}
        account: {type: string}
        partition: {type: string, default: short}
        nodes: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 64, default: 1}
        ntasksPerNode: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 192}
        gpusPerNode:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
          maximum: 4
          default: 0
        timeLimit:
          type: string
          description: Slurm time format, `[days-]hours:minutes:seconds`.
          pattern: '^(\d+-)?\d{1,2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$'
          default: "01:00:00"
        array: {type: [string, 'null'], examples: ["0-99%10", "1,3,5-7"]}
        callbackUrl: {type: [string, "null"], format: uri}
        script: {type: string, maxLength: 65536}
    Job:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'
        - type: object
          required: [jobId, state]
          properties:
            jobId: {type: string, readOnly: true}
            state: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobState'}
            submitTime: {type: string, format: date-time}
            startTime: {type: [string, 'null'], format: date-time}
            exitCode: {type: [integer, 'null'], examples: [0, 137]}
            efficiency:
              type: object
              description: CPU and memory efficiency as reported by `seff`, in percent.
              properties:
                cpu: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
                memory: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1.0e+2}
    Partition:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        idleNodes: {type: integer}
        maxTime: {type: string, examples: ["7-00:00:00"]}
        gres: {type: array, items: {type: string}, examples: [[ "gpu:a100:4" ]]}
    Usage:
      type: object
      properties:
        coreHours: {type: number}
        gpuHours: {type: number}
        fairshare: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: about:blank}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}

Scalable Krylov solvers & preconditioners for large sparse linear systems

[![CI](https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/fernsolve.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/fernsolve/) [![conda-forge](https://img.shields.io/conda/vn/conda-forge/fernsolve.svg)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/fernsolve) [![Docs](https://readthedocs.org/projects/fernsolve/badge/?version=stable)](https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.14012345.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14012345) **fernsolve** solves $Ax = b$ for large, sparse, (mostly) nonsymmetric $A$ on anything from a laptop to a few thousand MPI ranks. It provides restarted and pipelined Krylov methods (CG, GMRES($m$), BiCGStab($\ell$), IDR($s$)), a handful of robust preconditioners (ILU(k), ILUT, smoothed-aggregation AMG, block Jacobi) and mixed-precision iterative refinement, behind a C++20 core with Python bindings that accept anything `scipy.sparse` understands. It grew out of the Computational Mechanics group's need to solve pressure systems with ~10⁹ unknowns on the [larch cluster][larch] without writing PETSc boilerplate for every PhD project. If you already use PETSc or Trilinos and are happy with them, you probably don't need us :-) ## Features * Krylov methods - CG, preconditioned CG, block CG for multiple right-hand sides - GMRES($m$) with CGS2 or MGS orthogonalisation, flexible GMRES, and **pipelined GMRES** (Ghysels et al., 2013) for latency-bound runs - BiCGStab($\ell$) and IDR($s$) for when the $\mathcal{O}(mn)$ memory of GMRES hurts * Preconditioners: ILU(0), ILU(k), ILUT, block Jacobi with local ILU, smoothed-aggregation AMG * Distributed CSR matrices over MPI, with optional GPU offload of SpMV and triangular solves (CUDA or HIP) + Mixed-precision iterative refinement (`float32`/`bfloat16` factorisation, `float64` residuals) + Reproducible reductions: pass `deterministic=True` and you get bit-identical residual histories for a fixed number of ranks, at about 8 % extra cost Installation ------------ ```bash pip install fernsolve # CPU wheels with OpenMP, no MPI conda install -c conda-forge fernsolve "fernsolve=*=mpi_openmpi_*" ``` On HPC systems you almost certainly want to build against the site's MPI, so use Spack: ```console $ spack install fernsolve@2.4.1 +mpi +cuda cuda_arch=80 ^openmpi@4.1.6 ^openblas threads=openmp $ spack load fernsolve ``` or build from source (CMake ≥ 3.24, a C++20 compiler, MPI ≥ 3.1 and BLAS/LAPACK): git clone https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve.git && cd fernsolve cmake -S . -B build -DFERN_ENABLE_MPI=ON -DFERN_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build -j 16 && ctest --test-dir build -L unit pip install ./python --no-build-isolation ## Quick start ```python import numpy as np import scipy.sparse as sp from fernsolve import krylov, precond # 2-D Poisson on a 1000 x 1000 grid, n = 10**6 n = 1000 T = sp.diags([-1, 2, -1], [-1, 0, 1], shape=(n, n)) A = (sp.kron(sp.eye(n), T) + sp.kron(T, sp.eye(n))).tocsr() b = np.ones(A.shape[0]) M = precond.AMG(A, strength=0.25, max_levels=10) x, info = krylov.cg(A, b, M=M, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=200) print(info.iterations, info.residual_norm) # 14 8.7e-11 ``` The same in C++ (link against `fernsolve::fernsolve`): ```cpp #include int main(int argc, char** argv) { fern::mpi::environment env(argc, argv); auto A = fern::io::read_matrix_market("thermal2.mtx", env.world()); fern::dist_vector b(A.row_map(), 1.0), x(A.row_map(), 0.0); fern::precond::ilut M(A, {.fill = 20, .droptol = 1e-4}); auto info = fern::krylov::gmres(A, x, b, M, {.restart = 50, .rtol = 1e-8}); if (env.rank() == 0) std::printf("%d iterations, |r|/|b| = %.2e\n", info.iterations, info.relres); } ``` ## Changelog
=========

All notable changes to **fernsolve** are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres (mostly -- see the note under 2.0.0) to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

<!-- Maintainers: add entries under [Unreleased] in the same PR as the change. Reference the issue/PR number, not the commit hash. -->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- `fern::krylov::gmres_pipelined`: Ghysels–Vanroose pipelined GMRES($m$) that overlaps the global reduction with the next SpMV. On 64 nodes of larch this cuts time-to-solution for the replicated `thermal2` problem by ~31 % (#1043).
- Python: `fernsolve.callbacks.ResidualHistory` now also records the *true* residual $\|b - Ax_k\|_2$ every `check_every` iterations, next to the recursively updated one, so you can finally see when the two drift apart.
* HIP backend for the ILU(0) triangular solves (thanks to the AMD folks at the hackathon) 

### Changed
-   Default restart length for GMRES is now `restart=50` (was 30). For most SuiteSparse test matrices this reduces iteration counts by 10–25 %, at the cost of $\mathcal{O}(mn)$ extra memory; pass `restart=30` to get the old behaviour.
- The CMake option `FERN_USE_OPENMP` now defaults to `ON`.

### Fixed
- Loss of orthogonality in classical Gram–Schmidt with re-orthogonalisation (CGS2) when $\kappa(A) \gtrsim 10^{12}$. We now fall back to modified Gram–Schmidt for the offending Arnoldi step and emit a `ConvergenceWarning` instead of returning garbage. Reported by Dr. Ines Haldorsen with a beautifully minimal reproducer (#1031).
- `fern_mpi_finalize()` no longer deadlocks when called after a failed `MPI_Comm_split` (#1029)

## [2.4.1] - 2026-10-02

### Fixed

* Wheels for `manylinux_2_28_aarch64` were built without OpenMP, which made `fernsolve` up to 8× slower on the Grace nodes than the x86_64 build (#1019).
* Typo in the docstring of `fernsolve.precond.ILUT`: `droptol` is relative to the 2-norm of the row, not the ∞-norm.

## [2.4.0] - 2026-09-15

### Added

- **Mixed-precision iterative refinement** (`fernsolve.refine`): factorise in `float32` (or `bfloat16` on GPUs that support it), refine in `float64`. Converges whenever $\kappa_\infty(A)\,u_f < 1$, where $u_f$ is the unit roundoff of the factorisation precision; see Carson & Higham (2018) and the [user guide section on refinement][refine-docs].
- Block CG for multiple right-hand sides:

  ```python
  from fernsolve import krylov
  X, info = krylov.block_cg(A, B, M=precond, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=500)
  ```

- New `fernsolve-bench` command line tool.
  It replaces the old `scripts/bench.py` and writes results as CSV *and* as a Markdown table.

### Changed

1. Minimum supported versions: CMake 3.24, Python 3.10, NumPy 1.25, MPI 3.1.
2. `SolverInfo.converged` is now a `bool`, not an `int`. Code doing `if info.converged == 1:` still works; code doing `info.converged is 1` (please don't) does not.
3. Wheels are built against OpenBLAS 0.3.28.

### Deprecated
- `fernsolve.gmres(..., orthog="mgs")` -- pass `arnoldi=ArnoldiOptions(orthog="mgs")` instead. The keyword will be removed in 3.0.

### Performance

The CSR SpMV kernel for matrices with fewer than 8 nonzeros per row now uses a vectorised segmented reduction. Speed-ups on a single larch node (2× AMD EPYC 9654, 192 cores):

<!-- fmt: off -->
| matrix (SuiteSparse)  |      n |    nnz | 2.3.2 (GFlop/s) | 2.4.0 (GFlop/s) | speed-up |
|:----------------------|-------:|-------:|----------------:|----------------:|---------:|
| `G3_circuit`          |  1.59M |  7.66M |            41.2 |            63.9 |    1.55× |
| `thermal2`            |  1.23M |  8.58M |            44.0 |            61.3 |    1.39× |
| `ecology2`            |  1.00M |  5.00M |            37.5 |            66.1 |    1.76× |
<!-- fmt: on -->

## [2.3.2] - 2026-06-30
### Fixed
+ Segfault in `ilu0()` for matrices with an explicitly stored zero on the diagonal; we now raise `ZeroPivotError` with the offending row index.
+ Thread safety of the global `fern::set_verbosity()` (#987).

## [2.3.1] - 2026-05-12

### Fixed

- Regression from 2.3.0: `rtol` was treated as an absolute tolerance by `bicgstab` when `x0` was given. The stopping criterion is again
  $$\frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|b\|_2} \le \mathtt{rtol}$$
  for all solvers.
- `ResidualHistory.plot()` used a linear y-axis. It is log-scale again, as it should be for anything that converges geometrically.

## [2.3.0] - 2026-03-03

Big release, see the [migration notes](docs/migration/2.3.md) for details. Highlights:

* Algebraic multigrid preconditioner (`fernsolve.precond.AMG`, smoothed aggregation) with Chebyshev and $\ell_1$-Jacobi smoothers.
    * Coarse-grid solve via the direct solver of your choice (MUMPS, SuperLU_DIST, or our own dense LU for tiny coarse grids).
    * Setup is ~3× faster than PyAMG's on the same hierarchy, but we still recommend PyAMG for exploratory work.
* Dropped Python 3.8 and 3.9.

### Removed

- The `fernsolve.legacy` module (deprecated since 2.1).

## [2.0.0] - 2025-01-20

> **Note on versioning:** 2.0 broke the C ABI without breaking the C++ API, so strictly speaking only C users needed a major bump. We bumped everything to avoid confusing packagers (sorry, Spack maintainers).

First release under the new name (formerly `pyfern`).
The Python import name changed from `pyfern` to `fernsolve`; a shim package `pyfern==1.99` re-exports everything with a `DeprecationWarning`.

[2.4.1]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/compare/v2.4.0...v2.4.1
[2.4.0]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/compare/v2.3.2...v2.4.0

[2.3.1]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/compare/v2.3.0...v2.3.1
[2.3.0]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/compare/v2.0.0...v2.3.0
[2.0.0]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/releases/tag/v2.0.0
[refine-docs]: https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/refinement.html

2. `SolverInfo.converged` is now a `bool`, not an `int`. Code doing `if info.converged == 1:` still works; code doing `info.converged is 1` (please don't) does not.
3. Wheels are built against OpenBLAS 0.3.28.

### Deprecated
- `fernsolve.gmres(..., orthog="mgs")` -- pass `arnoldi=ArnoldiOptions(orthog="mgs")` instead. The keyword will be removed in 3.0.

### Performance

The CSR SpMV kernel for matrices with fewer than 8 nonzeros per row now uses a vectorised segmented reduction. Speed-ups on a single larch node (2× AMD EPYC 9654, 192 cores):

<!-- fmt: off -->
| matrix (SuiteSparse)  |      n |    nnz | 2.3.2 (GFlop/s) | 2.4.0 (GFlop/s) | speed-up |
|:----------------------|-------:|-------:|----------------:|----------------:|---------:|
| `G3_circuit`          |  1.59M |  7.66M |            41.2 |            63.9 |    1.55× |
| `thermal2`            |  1.23M |  8.58M |            44.0 |            61.3 |    1.39× |
| `ecology2`            |  1.00M |  5.00M |            37.5 |            66.1 |    1.76× |
<!-- fmt: on -->

## [2.3.2] - 2026-06-30
### Fixed
+ Segfault in `ilu0()` for matrices with an explicitly stored zero on the diagonal; we now raise `ZeroPivotError` with the offending row index.
+ Thread safety of the global `fern::set_verbosity()` (#987).

## [2.3.1] - 2026-05-12

### Fixed

- Regression from 2.3.0: `rtol` was treated as an absolute tolerance by `bicgstab` when `x0` was given. The stopping criterion is again
  $$\frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|b\|_2} \le \mathtt{rtol}$$
  for all solvers.
- `ResidualHistory.plot()` used a linear y-axis. It is log-scale again, as it should be for anything that converges geometrically.

## [2.3.0] - 2026-03-03

Big release, see the [migration notes](docs/migration/2.3.md) for details. Highlights:

* Algebraic multigrid preconditioner (`fernsolve.precond.AMG`, smoothed aggregation) with Chebyshev and $\ell_1$-Jacobi smoothers.
    * Coarse-grid solve via the direct solver of your choice (MUMPS, SuperLU_DIST, or our own dense LU for tiny coarse grids).
    * Setup is ~3× faster than PyAMG's on the same hierarchy, but we still recommend PyAMG for exploratory work.
* Dropped Python 3.8 and 3.9.

### Removed

- The `fernsolve.legacy` module (deprecated since 2.1).

## [2.0.0] - 2025-01-20

> **Note on versioning:** 2.0 broke the C ABI without breaking the C++ API, so strictly speaking only C users needed a major bump. We bumped everything to avoid confusing packagers (sorry, Spack maintainers).

First release under the new name (formerly `pyfern`).
The Python import name changed from `pyfern` to `fernsolve`; a shim package `pyfern==1.99` re-exports everything with a `DeprecationWarning`.

# Contributing to varcall

Thanks for helping out! `varcall` is the germline short-variant calling pipeline (FASTQ → aligned CRAM → gVCF → joint-called, filtered VCF) used by the Mensah lab and the Northfield Genomics Core. It is written in Nextflow DSL2, with small Python and R helpers under `bin/`, and runs on the larch Slurm cluster, on the lab's Kubernetes namespace and -- with some patience -- on a laptop.

This document is for people *changing* the pipeline. If you only want to run it, read [README.md](README.md) and `docs/usage.md` instead.

**Contents**

1. [Ground rules](#ground-rules)
2. [Development environment](#development-environment)
3. [Tests](#tests)
4. [Adding or updating a module](#adding-or-updating-a-module)
5) [Commit messages and merge requests](#commit-messages-and-merge-requests)
6) [Releasing](#releasing)

Ground rules
------------

* Never commit patient-identifiable data. Test data under `tests/data/` is either synthetic or from the public **GIAB HG002** sample, downsampled to ~2× around chr20:10,000,000-12,000,000. If you are not 100 % sure a file is OK to share, ask Dr. Mensah *before* pushing; rewriting git history is painful and does not un-leak anything.
* All changes go through a merge request against `dev`; `main` only moves on releases.
- Results must stay reproducible: an MR that changes any output VCF needs a justification in its description and an updated truth set (see [Tests](#tests)).
*   Be kind in reviews. Most contributors are PhD students with a thesis to write.

## Development environment

We use [pixi](https://pixi.sh) for Nextflow itself and the Python/R helpers, and containers (Apptainer on larch, Docker elsewhere) for the bioinformatics tools:

```bash
git clone git@git.northfield.ac.uk:mensah-lab/varcall.git
cd varcall
pixi install            # nextflow, nf-test, python 3.12, R 4.4, pre-commit
pixi run pre-commit install
```

On larch, do this on a login node but run anything heavier than `nf-test` in an interactive job (`salloc -p short -c 8 --mem=32G -t 2:00:00`). The login nodes kill processes that use more than 4 GB of RAM, and you *will* hit that with GATK.

> [!WARNING]
> Do **not** keep the Apptainer cache in your home directory: home has a 50 GB quota and a single DeepVariant image is 6 GB. Put
> `export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=/scratch/$USER/.apptainer` in your `~/.bashrc`.

## Tests ##

There are three layers of tests:

1. **Unit tests** for the helper scripts (`pytest` for Python, `testthat` for R):

   ```bash
   pixi run pytest bin/tests -q
   pixi run Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("bin/tests/testthat")'
   ```
2. **Module tests** with [nf-test](https://www.nf-test.com/), one per module under `modules/local/*/tests/`. Run all of them with `nf-test test --profile apptainer`, or only the one you changed:
    ```bash
    nf-test test modules/local/deepvariant/tests/main.nf.test --profile apptainer
    ```
3. **End-to-end** test on the GIAB subset. It takes ~25 min on 4 nodes and runs nightly in CI, but please run it yourself if you touch anything in `subworkflows/`:

       sbatch --wait tests/e2e/run_e2e.sbatch
       python tests/e2e/compare_to_truth.py results/e2e/HG002.vcf.gz --truth tests/data/HG002_chr20_truth.vcf.gz --min-f1 0.995

   The comparison uses `hap.py`. An MR may lower SNV F1 by at most 0.001 and indel F1 by at most 0.003 without a discussion; anything more needs sign-off from the Core.

### Making new test data

If you need reads for a new region, downsample from the full 35× HG002 BAM rather than committing big files. To get a target coverage $c_t$ from an original coverage $c_0$, keep each read pair with probability $p = c_t / c_0$, e.g. $p = 2/35 \approx 0.057$ for 2×:

```bash
samtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 HG002.GRCh38.35x.bam chr20:10000000-12000000 > HG002_chr20_2x.bam
```

Expected coverage after subsampling is $c_t$ only on average; for small regions check it with `mosdepth` and redraw with another seed if it is off by more than 10 %.

The `Makefile` in `tests/data/` regenerates everything (recipes must be indented with a tab, not spaces):

```make
HG002_chr20_2x.bam: $(SRC_BAM)
⇥samtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 $< chr20:10000000-12000000 > $@
⇥samtools index $@
```

## Adding or updating a module

Every module lives in `modules/local/<tool>/` and needs a `main.nf`, a `meta.yml` and at least one nf-test. CI validates `meta.yml` against `assets/schema_module.json`, so stick to this layout:

```yaml
name: deepvariant_callvariants
description:  Call variants from a CRAM with DeepVariant (on a GPU if one is available)
keywords: [ variant calling, deep learning,gvcf ]
tools:
    - deepvariant:
        description: "DeepVariant is an analysis pipeline that uses a deep neural network to call genetic variants from next-generation DNA sequencing data."
        homepage: https://github.com/google/deepvariant
        licence: ['BSD-3-Clause']
input:
  - meta:
      type: map
      description: Groovy map with sample information, e.g. `[ id:'HG002', sex:'XY' ]`
  - cram: {type: file, pattern: "*.cram"}
output:
  - vcf: {type: file, pattern: "*.vcf.gz"}
  - gvcf:
      type: file
      pattern: "*.g.vcf.gz"
authors: ["J. Ortiz", 'K. Mensah']
```

Please **don't** pin tool versions in `meta.yml` the way the old template did; they go stale immediately and the container tag is the single source of truth:

```yaml fmt: skip
tools:
  - deepvariant:
      version:   1.6.1     # <- no!
      container: "google/deepvariant:1.6.1-gpu"
```

<details>
<summary>Why Nextflow and not Snakemake?</summary>

We get asked this a lot. Short answer: the Core's other pipelines are Nextflow, and the Kubernetes executor was the deciding factor back in 2022. Long answer: see the discussion in [issue 14](https://git.northfield.ac.uk/mensah-lab/varcall/-/issues/14).

</details>

## Commit messages and merge requests

We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), mostly so that `git-cliff` can write the changelog for us:

| type | use it for | bumps |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `feat` | new module, new parameter | minor |
| `fix` | wrong results, crashes | patch |
| `perf` | faster or leaner, **identical** output | patch |
| `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `test` | everything else | -- |

When you open an MR, GitLab pre-fills this template (`.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md`). Please actually fill it in:

````markdown
## What does this change?

<!-- one or two sentences, plus the issue number -->

## Checklist
- [ ] `nf-test test` passes locally (or on larch: paste the Slurm job ID)
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under *Unreleased*
-  [ ] If outputs change: hap.py comparison attached and F1 deltas filled in below
* [ ] Reviewed by someone who did not write it

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| SNV F1 |  |  |
| indel F1 | | |
````

## Releasing

Only maintainers (currently J. Ortiz and K. Mensah) cut releases:

0. Make sure the nightly end-to-end run on `dev` is green.
1. Bump `manifest.version` in `nextflow.config` and move the *Unreleased* changelog entries under the new version.
2. Merge `dev` into `main`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and push the tag; CI builds and pushes the containers.
3. Announce the release in the Core's Teams channel with a link to the changelog.\
   If any output changed, say so explicitly.

By contributing you agree that your contributions are licensed under the MIT licence[^licence].

***

[^licence]: The containers we build include tools under other licences (GATK and DeepVariant are BSD-3-Clause, `samtools` is MIT/Expat). That does not affect the licence of the pipeline code itself.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ---
# jupyter:
#   jupytext:
#     formats: ipynb,py:percent
#     text_representation:
#       extension: .py
#       format_name: percent
#       format_version: '1.3'
#   kernelspec:
#     display_name: cmorph-pp (py3.12)
#     language: python
#     name: cmorph-pp
# ---

# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
# # SST anomalies from CMIP6 `tos` on a common 1° grid
#
# Post-processing step 2 of the **cmorph-pp** chain (Climate Analytics Group, Northfield). Takes native-grid monthly `tos` from the ESGF mirror, regrids it conservatively to a regular 1° grid with xESMF, and writes anomalies relative to the 1981–2010 climatology. For every member the anomaly in month $m$ of year $y$ at cell $(i,j)$ is
#
# $$
# T'_{ij}(y,m) = T_{ij}(y,m) - \frac{1}{30}\sum_{y'=1981}^{2010} T_{ij}(y',m),
# $$
#
# and the global mean is area-weighted over ocean cells of the *target* grid, i.e. $\overline{T'} = \sum_{ij} A_{ij} T'_{ij} / \sum_{ij} A_{ij}$ (cf. Eyring et al. 2016 for the CMIP6 protocol).
#
# Run it interactively (Jupytext pairs it with `sst_anomalies.ipynb`) or as a batch job:
#
#     sbatch -p short -c 32 --mem=120G --wrap "python sst_anomalies.py --source-id CanESM5 --experiment ssp245"
#
# * Inputs are **never** modified; outputs go to `$CMORPH_OUT/<source_id>/<experiment>/`.
# * Regridding weights are cached in `$CMORPH_WEIGHTS` (one file per source grid, ~200 MB each), reuse them!
#   Recomputing the weights for a 0.25° ocean grid takes ~20 min on 32 cores.

# %%
#| label: imports
#| jupyter: {source_hidden: true, outputs_hidden: False}
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import dask
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
import xesmf as xe
from dask.distributed import Client, LocalCluster

__version__ = "2026.11.0"
log = logging.getLogger("cmorph.sst")

# %%
#| label: parameters
#| tags:
#|     - parameters
#| params:
#|   source_id:   CanESM5
#|   experiment: ssp245
#|   members: [r1i1p1f1, r2i1p1f1,r3i1p1f1]
#|   grid: "1x1"
#|   ref_period: [ 1981, 2010 ]
#| description: >
#|   Defaults for interactive use only. The batch wrapper overrides all of these from the command line,
#|   so do not put anything site-specific (paths!) in here.
SOURCE_ID = "CanESM5"
EXPERIMENT = "ssp245"
MEMBERS = ["r1i1p1f1", "r2i1p1f1", "r3i1p1f1"]
GRID = "1x1"
METHOD = "conservative_normed"
REF_START, REF_END = 1981, 2010
MIN_OCEAN_FRAC=0.5  # fmt: skip

# Ocean model + coordinate names per source_id. Hand-aligned on purpose; ruff, keep out.
# fmt: off
NATIVE_GRIDS = {
    #  source_id          ocean model       nominal res.   lon / lat names
    "CanESM5":          ("NEMO3.4.1",      "1deg",        ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "MPI-ESM1-2-HR":    ("MPIOM1.63",      "0.4deg",      ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "IPSL-CM6A-LR":     ("NEMO-OPA",       "1deg",        ("nav_lon",   "nav_lat")),
    "UKESM1-0-LL":      ("NEMO3.6",        "1deg",        ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "GFDL-CM4":         ("MOM6",           "0.25deg",     ("lon",       "lat")),
}
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = r"""
## Notes

Anomalies are computed **per member** and only then averaged, never the other way round: when members have different missing months, the climatology of the ensemble mean is not the ensemble mean of the climatologies.

Drift correction (`--dedrift`) fits a quadratic $d(t) = a + b\,t + c\,t^2$ to the matching `piControl` segment and subtracts it. Use it for models whose $|\Delta T|$ drift exceeds 0.1 K per century, cf. Table 2 of the validation report.

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--grid` | `1x1` | target grid, `1x1` or `0.25x0.25` |
| `--method` | `conservative_normed` | any xESMF method; *bilinear* is wrong for SST near coasts |
| `--dedrift` | off | subtract the piControl drift |
"""

# Global attributes for every output file (CF-1.10 + our provenance fields).
# fmt: json
GLOBAL_ATTRS = """
{"Conventions": "CF-1.10", "institution": "University of Northfield, Climate Analytics Group",
   "source": "CMIP6 tos, regridded with xESMF", "license": "CC BY 4.0",
 "references": "Lindqvist et al. (2026), cmorph-pp validation report", "product_version": "2026.11.0"}
"""


def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cmorph-sst", description="Regrid CMIP6 tos and compute SST anomalies.",
                                epilog=EPILOG, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--source-id", default=SOURCE_ID, choices=sorted(NATIVE_GRIDS))
    p.add_argument("--experiment", default=EXPERIMENT, choices=["historical", "ssp126", "ssp245", "ssp370", "ssp585"])
    p.add_argument("--members", nargs="+", default=MEMBERS)
    p.add_argument("--grid", default=GRID, choices=["1x1", "0.25x0.25"])
    p.add_argument("--method", default=METHOD)
    p.add_argument("--ref-start", type=int, default=REF_START)
    p.add_argument("--ref-end", type=int, default=REF_END)
    p.add_argument("--dedrift", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    return p.parse_args(argv)


def start_dask() -> Client:
    """Size a LocalCluster from the Slurm allocation, if there is one."""
    ncpu = int(os.environ.get("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", os.cpu_count() or 4))
    nworkers = max(ncpu // 4, 1)
    mem = os.environ.get("SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE")  # MB
    cluster = LocalCluster(n_workers=nworkers, threads_per_worker=4,
                           memory_limit=f"{int(mem) // nworkers}MB" if mem else "auto",
                           local_directory=os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp"))
    return Client(cluster)


def open_member(source_id: str, experiment: str, member: str) -> xr.Dataset:
    root = Path(os.environ.get("CMIP6_ROOT", "/data/cmip6")) / "CMIP6"
    activity = "CMIP" if experiment == "historical" else "ScenarioMIP"
    files = sorted(root.glob(f"{activity}/*/{source_id}/{experiment}/{member}/Omon/tos/*/latest/*.nc"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no tos files for {source_id}/{experiment}/{member} under {root}")
    return xr.open_mfdataset(files, combine="by_coords", chunks={"time": 120}, use_cftime=True, parallel=True)


# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown
# ## Regridding
#
# xESMF's `conservative_normed` renormalises by the unmasked fraction of each target cell, which is what we want for a field that only exists over the ocean.  Plain `conservative` biases coastal cells low (towards 0 °C!) because land counts as zero.
# Weights depend only on the source grid, so they are cached per `source_id`.

# %%
#| label: regrid
#| echo: true
#| # fmt: compact
#| tags:
#|   - core
#|   - slow
def regrid(ds: xr.Dataset, grid_spec: str, method: str, source_id: str) -> xr.DataArray:
    d = {"1x1": 1.0, "0.25x0.25": 0.25}[grid_spec]
    target = xe.util.grid_global(d, d, cf=True)
    wdir = Path(os.environ.get("CMORPH_WEIGHTS", "/scratch/cmorph/weights"))
    wfile = wdir / f"{source_id}_{method}_{grid_spec}.nc"
    regridder = xe.Regridder(ds, target, method, periodic=True, ignore_degenerate=True,
                             filename=str(wfile), reuse_weights=wfile.exists())
    return regridder(ds["tos"], keep_attrs=True)


def anomalies(tos: xr.DataArray, ref: tuple[int, int]) -> xr.DataArray:
    clim = tos.sel(time=slice(f"{ref[0]}-01-01", f"{ref[1]}-12-31")).groupby("time.month").mean("time")
    return (tos.groupby("time.month") - clim).drop_vars("month")


def global_mean(da: xr.DataArray) -> xr.DataArray:
    w = np.cos(np.deg2rad(da.lat))   # regular lat-lon => cell area ∝ cos(lat)
    return da.weighted(w).mean(("lat", "lon"))


def provenance_note(args: argparse.Namespace, n_files: int) -> str:
    """README.md written next to the output files."""
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
# Provenance: {args.source_id} / {args.experiment}

Generated by `cmorph-sst` {__version__} on {now:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC from {len(args.members)} member(s) ({", ".join(args.members)}) and {n_files} input files. Regridded to the {args.grid} grid with xESMF `{args.method}`; anomalies are relative to {args.ref_start}–{args.ref_end}.

* drift correction: {"quadratic fit to piControl" if args.dedrift else "none"}
* software:   xarray {xr.__version__}, xesmf {xe.__version__}, dask {dask.__version__}, numpy {np.__version__}
"""


# %%
#| label: main
#| eval: false
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING - 10 * args.verbose, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    client = start_dask()
    log.info("dask dashboard: %s", client.dashboard_link)
    out = Path(os.environ.get("CMORPH_OUT", "/scratch/cmorph/out")) / args.source_id / args.experiment
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    attrs = json.loads(GLOBAL_ATTRS) | {"history": f"{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%FT%TZ} cmorph-sst {' '.join(sys.argv[1:])}"}
    n_files = 0
    for member in args.members:
        ds = open_member(args.source_id, args.experiment, member)
        n_files += len(ds.encoding.get("source", "x").split(","))
        anom = anomalies(regrid(ds, args.grid, args.method, args.source_id), (args.ref_start, args.ref_end))
        anom = anom.rename("tos_anom").assign_attrs(units="K", long_name="sea surface temperature anomaly")
        anom.to_dataset().assign_attrs(attrs).to_netcdf(out / f"tos_anom_{member}_{args.grid}.nc",
                                                         encoding={"tos_anom": {"zlib": True, "complevel": 4}})
        log.info("%s: global-mean anomaly in last year %.3f K", member, float(global_mean(anom)[-12:].mean()))
    (out / "README.md").write_text(provenance_note(args, n_files), encoding="utf-8")
    client.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
#SBATCH --job-name=covqc
#SBATCH --partition=short
#SBATCH --array=1-96%24
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=01:30:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out

# coverage_qc.R -- per-sample coverage QC from mosdepth output (Mensah lab, varcall pipeline)
#
# Usage, one array task per sample (the sample list has one path prefix per line):
#   sbatch --export=ALL,SAMPLES=batches/2026_11.txt bin/coverage_qc.R
# or render the whole batch as an HTML report:
#   quarto render bin/coverage_qc.R -P batch:2026_11

#' # Coverage QC for a sequencing batch
#'
#' This script doubles as a `knitr::spin()` report: lines starting with `#'` are Markdown and `#|` lines are chunk options.

#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| message:   FALSE
#| warning: no
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glue)
})
options(datatable.print.nrows = 20, warn = 1)

# fmt: markdown
# ## QC thresholds
#
# A sample **passes** if all of the following hold (agreed with the Genomics Core in Nov. 2025):
#
# | metric | threshold | why |
# |---|---|---|
# | median autosomal coverage | ≥ 30× | DeepVariant sensitivity drops quickly below ~25× (cf. Poplin et al. 2018) |
# | fraction of bases ≥ 20× | ≥ 0.90 | |
# | chrX / autosome ratio | consistent with the reported sex | catches sample swaps |
# | coverage CV | ≤ 0.35 | a high CV usually means GC bias or degraded DNA |
#
# Samples between 20× and 30× are flagged `LOW` but still called; below 20× they `FAIL` and need re-sequencing.
# The coefficient of variation is computed over 1 kb bins as $\mathrm{CV} = \sigma / \mu$, excluding bins in the ENCODE blacklist (Amemiya et al. 2019).
THRESHOLDS <- list(
  median_cov  = 30,     # LOW below this
  hard_min    = 20,     # FAIL below this
  frac_ge20   = 0.90,
  cv_max      = 0.35,
  x_ratio_xx  = c(0.85, 1.15),
  x_ratio_xy  = c(0.40, 0.60)
)

# fmt: markdown
help_md <- r"---[
Per-sample coverage QC for **varcall** batches.

Reads `<prefix>.mosdepth.summary.txt` and `<prefix>.regions.bed.gz` (1 kb bins) for every sample listed in `$SAMPLES` and writes `<prefix>.covqc.tsv`. When run as a Slurm array job, task *i* processes line *i* of the sample list; otherwise all samples are processed one after the other, which takes about 40 s per 30× genome.

-   `SAMPLES`: path to the sample list (default `samples.txt`)
-   `SEX_TABLE`: optional TSV with columns `sample` and `sex` (`XX`/`XY`) from the sample sheet
]---"

# Batch summary, posted as a comment on the sequencing-run issue in GitLab.
# Placeholders are filled by glue::glue(), hence the {braces}.
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
summary_template <- r"(
## Coverage QC: batch {batch}

{n_pass} of {n_total} samples passed, {n_low} are `LOW` (20–30×) and {n_fail} `FAIL` (< 20×). Median coverage across the batch was {median_cov}× (IQR {iqr_lo}–{iqr_hi}×). Samples flagged `SEX_MISMATCH` must be checked against the sample sheet before anything else is done with them, since a swap always affects two samples.

{fail_table}

Re-sequencing requests go to the Core via the usual form, please link this issue. Plots: `{plot_path}`
)"

# Appended to each task's log so a single sample can be re-run outside Slurm.
# fmt: r
rerun_snippet <- "
source('bin/coverage_qc.R')
res <- qc_sample(prefix='%s',  sex = NA)
print(res[ , .(sample,median_cov,frac_ge20,cv,status)])
"

read_mosdepth <- function(prefix) {
  summ <- fread(paste0(prefix, ".mosdepth.summary.txt"))
  bins <- fread(paste0(prefix, ".regions.bed.gz"), col.names = c("chrom", "start", "end", "depth"))
  list(summary = summ, bins = bins)
}

qc_sample <- function(prefix, sex = NA_character_, thresholds = THRESHOLDS) {
  md <- read_mosdepth(prefix)
  auto <- md$bins[chrom %in% paste0("chr", 1:22)]
  med <- median(auto$depth)
  cv <- sd(auto$depth) / mean(auto$depth)
  frac20 <- mean(auto$depth >= 20)
  x_ratio <- median(md$bins[chrom == "chrX"]$depth) / med
  expected <- switch(sex %||% "unknown", XX = thresholds$x_ratio_xx, XY = thresholds$x_ratio_xy, c(0, Inf))
  status <- fcase(
    med < thresholds$hard_min, "FAIL",
    x_ratio < expected[1] | x_ratio > expected[2], "SEX_MISMATCH",
    med < thresholds$median_cov | frac20 < thresholds$frac_ge20 | cv > thresholds$cv_max, "LOW",
    default = "PASS"
  )
  data.table(sample = basename(prefix), median_cov = med, frac_ge20 = frac20, cv = cv,
             x_ratio = x_ratio, status = status)
}

#' ## Run
#'
#' In array mode exactly one sample is processed and the script exits; the summary and plots below are only produced when the whole batch is processed in one go (interactively or via `quarto render`).

#| label: run
#| eval: !expr '!interactive() || nzchar(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES"))'
samples <- readLines(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES", "samples.txt"))
task <- Sys.getenv("SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID", unset = NA)
if (!is.na(task)) {
  prefix <- samples[as.integer(task)]
  res <- qc_sample(prefix)
  fwrite(res, paste0(prefix, ".covqc.tsv"), sep = "\t")
  message(sprintf(rerun_snippet, prefix))
  quit(save = "no", status = 0L)
}
res <- rbindlist(lapply(samples, qc_sample))

#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Median autosomal coverage per sample. Dashed: 30× target; dotted: 20× hard minimum."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:  4
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of median coverage for every sample in the batch, coloured by QC status.
ggplot(res, aes(reorder(sample, median_cov), median_cov, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = THRESHOLDS$median_cov, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = THRESHOLDS$hard_min, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(PASS = "#1b9e77", LOW = "#d95f02", FAIL = "#7570b3", SEX_MISMATCH = "#e7298a")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "median coverage (×)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 6))

#| label: summary
#| results: asis
#| R.options: {knitr.kable.NA: ''}
batch <- Sys.getenv("BATCH", basename(tools::file_path_sans_ext(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES", "batch"))))
q <- quantile(res$median_cov, c(0.25, 0.75))
fails <- res[status != "PASS"]
fail_table <- if (nrow(fails)) paste(knitr::kable(fails, digits = 2), collapse = "\n") else "_No samples flagged._"
summary_md <- glue(summary_template,
  n_pass = sum(res$status == "PASS"), n_total = nrow(res),
  n_low = sum(res$status == "LOW"), n_fail = sum(res$status == "FAIL"),
  median_cov = round(median(res$median_cov), 1), iqr_lo = round(q[[1]], 1), iqr_hi = round(q[[2]], 1),
  plot_path = file.path("qc", batch, "coverage.png"))
writeLines(summary_md, file.path("qc", batch, "summary.md"))
cat(summary_md)
